question.text: The solubility of a salt of weak acid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced separators="|"><mi>AB</mi></mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>at</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>pH</mi><mn>3</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>is</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>mol</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> . The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></math> is ____. (Given that the value of solubility product of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>AB</mi><mfenced separators="|"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi>sp</mi></msub></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi></math>, and the value of ionization constant of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>HB</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mi>Ka</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
S=KspH+Ka+1=2×10-1010-310-8+1≃2×10-5
=4.47×10-3M.
